name: workable-mcp
description: Workable (jobs): me, search, get_posting. Every tool maps to a documented endpoint.

platform_mcp_workable_api_token.title: PLATFORM_MCP_WORKABLE_API_TOKEN
platform_mcp_workable_api_token.description: Workable API access token (Settings > Integrations > Apps / API access token) with the r_jobs scope; sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. It is the employer account's token.

platform_mcp_workable_subdomain.title: PLATFORM_MCP_WORKABLE_SUBDOMAIN
platform_mcp_workable_subdomain.description: The Workable account subdomain, e.g. 'groove-tech' in https://groove-tech.workable.com.

tools.name: me
tools.description: GET /spi/v3/accounts/:subdomain 'Returns the specified account' (id, name, subdomain, description, url). Required scope: r_jobs.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Employer ATS API: GET /spi/v3/jobs?state=published lists the account's OWN published jobs (not a cross-company search). There is no keyword or location filter, so query/location are not sent — filter client-side. limit: 'By default results are limited to 50 … cannot be more than 100'. Paging is a since_id cursor (paging.next URL), which this tool does not follow: page is not sent, so only the first page is returned — raise limit to 100 for larger accounts. id is the job shortcode (use it with get_posting); salary_currency is lower-case (e.g. 'eur'); department, workplace_type, application_url, shortlink and location parts are in raw.

tools.name: get_posting
tools.description: GET /spi/v3/jobs/:shortcode 'will return the full job JSON object'; description is full_description (HTML); requirements, benefits, employment_type and application_url are in raw.
